newsitem.title: GERMANY: ProSieben says future of ads lies in TV, online.
newsitem.headline: ProSieben says future of ads lies in TV, online.

text.p: The future of television advertising lies in a mixture of new technology and traditional TV commercials, German television group ProSieben Media AG said.

"Advertising in the year 2000 will be a combination of mass ads on television, information offers on teletext and fully interactive options on online media," ProSieben board member and marketing director Michael Woelfle told Reuters in an interview on Monday.

Woelfle said the current format of TV ads was likely to continue to dominate the industry, drawing 90 to 95 percent of advertising investment. The ProSieben group plans to expand its marketing activities in the new media, he added.
Digital television represents a "quantum leap" in the ability to monitor ads' effectiveness in reaching their target groups. Woelfle said.
"Viewer patterns will be able to be traced precisely and not just estimated on the basis of panels," Woelfle said of the digital TV.
Woelfle called for the loosening of Germany's famously restrictive TV ad regulations, in which the number and length of commercial breaks are strictly limited.
"No private station in Germany wants to boost the volume of advertising, but everyone would like to see more flexibility," Woelfle said.

He added that he expected online advertising would need at least another five years to become a significant force in the industry, time that should be used to develop new production techniques and ad concepts specialised for a cyberspace format.

The ProSieben group posted its first significant turnover from online advertising in the second quarter of 1997 and expects turnover this year to reach the single-digit million mark range, Woelfle said.
He said he foresees the potential for 20 to 25 percent growth for the group and its two stations, ProSieben and Kabel 1, in net advertising turnover in the next two to three years.
